title: Home-Visit Settlement Charge — Open Service Charges of a Mobile In-Home Collection Visit
content:
*Patient Financial Services calculation clause — Specimen Collection Appointments.*

**Clause.** The home-visit settlement charge is the total of the charges standing open on the visit, that is its trip, additional-patient and weekend charges and any late-change charge, where a charge stands open for its assessed amount less any waiver or payment posted against it plus any refund of such a payment, rounded to the cent.

## The open total, charge by charge

Each of the four charges of a Mobile In-Home Collection Visit stands open, on the visit's fee record, for:

> its assessed amount, less any waiver posted against it, less any payment posted against it, plus any refund of such a payment.

The open total is the sum of the four open amounts: the trip charge, the additional-patient (household) charge, the weekend charge and the late-change charge (posted as a late-cancellation fee). A charge that was never assessed on the visit stands open for nothing.

## Percentages and rounding

Percentage allowances on a settlement are first added together into one total allowance, and the open total is reduced once by that total allowance, taken as a percentage of the open total; the allowances never act one after another. The settlement charge is rounded to the cent only once, at the end.

## Worked figures (hypothetical fee records)

| Charge on the visit | Assessed | Waived | Paid | Refunded | Stands open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trip charge | 95.00 | — | — | — | 95.00 |
| Additional-patient charge | 70.00 | — | — | — | 70.00 |
| Weekend charge | 35.00 | — | — | — | 35.00 |
| Late-change charge | 40.00 | 40.00 | — | — | 0.00 |
| **Open total** | | | | | **200.00** |

On this record the home-visit settlement charge is 200.00.

A second hypothetical record — a trip charge of 75.00 that was paid and then refunded, nothing else assessed — stands open for 75.00 less 75.00 plus 75.00, that is 75.00.

Illustration of the percentage rule with invented percentages: two allowances of 4 percent and 6 percent on an open total of 200.00 are added into one total allowance of 10 percent; 10 percent of 200.00 is 20.00; the result is 180.00.
